title: Signed comparison of the horseshoe and explicit Tor kernel boundaries
statement: Let R be a commutative ring, M,F,N be R-modules, and q:F → N a surjective linear map. Write K=ker(q). Let A,B,C be projective resolutions of K,F,N, with complex maps a:A → B and b:B → C satisfying ab=0, compatible with the kernel inclusion and q on augmentations. Assume each degree sequence admits a splitting, and let hS be a proof that the tensored sequence is short exact. The composite of the Tor1(N,M)-to-H1(C tensor M) isomorphism, the homology connecting map of this tensored sequence, the degree-zero homology-to-opcycles inclusion for A tensor M, and the augmentation-induced map A.fromLeftDerivedZero' equals the negative of the constructed torKernelBoundary. The boundary is the fixed real construction of [def-sc-p1-tor-kernel-boundary-construction]; the connecting morphism is that of [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact].

source.place: Algebra Tags 00M0 and 00LZ; Homology Tag 0111 (snake construction of the homology connecting map); explicit sign comparison fills the computation in the original exact-left-kernel proof plan.

proof.text: Let P be the chosen resolution of N and c:P → C a comparison lifting the identity. In degrees zero and one compose c with the sections of b to define l0,l1. Set v=l1 dB-dP l0 and t=v r0, where r0 is the retraction of a0. The chain identity gives v b0=0, and the splitting identity gives t a0=v. Let e0=l0 epsilonB. The augmentation identities give e0 q=epsilonP and t epsilonA i=-dP e0.

The difference between the chosen augmentation lift e and e0 factors through K; define k by codomain restriction. The preceding identity implies D+t epsilonA=dP k, where D is torKernelDifferential. Tensoring and composing with the cycle inclusion kills dP k. Thus on tensor cycles, t followed by epsilonA is the negative of D. All these maps are constructed from the given splitting data and the proved surjection; no unproved existence theorem chooses data.

For a cycle z of P tensor M, set x3=(c1 tensor 1)z, x2=(l1 tensor 1)z and x1=(t tensor 1)z. The chain identity says x3 is a cycle, b1 x2=x3, and a0 x1=dB x2. Mathlib ShortExact.δ_apply gives that the connecting map sends [x3] to [x1]. Composing the homology projection in degree zero with the homology-to-opcycles map and A.fromLeftDerivedZero' equals cycle inclusion followed by the tensored augmentation, by homology_π_ι and pOpcycles_comp_fromLeftDerivedZero'. The cycle equality of the previous step therefore gives the signed boundary equality. Cancel the epic homology projection and the Tor-to-homology isomorphism, using resolution comparison naturality for the identity.

theorem tor_kernel_boundary_horseshoe_comparison
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (M : ModuleCat.{u} R)
    (F N : ModuleCat.{u} R) (q : F →ₗ[R] N) (hq : Function.Surjective q)
    (A : ProjectiveResolution (ModuleCat.of R (LinearMap.ker q)))
    (B : ProjectiveResolution F) (C : ProjectiveResolution N)
    (a : A.complex ⟶ B.complex) (b : B.complex ⟶ C.complex) (w : a ≫ b = 0)
    (ha : a.f 0 ≫ B.π.f 0 = A.π.f 0 ≫ ModuleCat.ofHom (LinearMap.ker q).subtype)
    (hb : b.f 0 ≫ C.π.f 0 = B.π.f 0 ≫ ModuleCat.ofHom q)
    (hs : ∀ n, Nonempty ((ShortComplex.mk a b w).map
      (HomologicalComplex.eval (ModuleCat R) (ComplexShape.down ℕ) n)).Splitting)
    (hS : ((ShortComplex.mk a b w).map
      (((MonoidalCategory.tensoringRight (ModuleCat R)).obj M).mapHomologicalComplex
        (ComplexShape.down ℕ))).ShortExact) :
    (C.isoLeftDerivedObj ((MonoidalCategory.tensoringRight (ModuleCat R)).obj M) 1).hom ≫
      hS.δ 1 0 (by simp) ≫
      (ChainComplex.isoHomologyι₀ _).hom ≫
      A.fromLeftDerivedZero' ((MonoidalCategory.tensoringRight (ModuleCat R)).obj M) =
        -ModuleCat.ofHom (torKernelBoundary M F N q hq)
